compiled_state.title: [brainstorm]: New git-ref pattern introduced without workflow-trigger audit -> Existing CI workflows skip the new pattern silently
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** 5d5f6e904dd3c8d731c8fcd956fb288790b884c9
* **Skill:** plugins/dso/skills/brainstorm/SKILL.md

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** Sub-Agent Blocker (planning-model defect)

**Filed by d076 post-mortem analysis (`docs/findings/d076-postmortem-analysis.md`) — implementation deferred to a remediation sprint.**

#### Expected Behavior

When an epic introduces a new git ref pattern (e.g., story/**, fix/**, bug-batch/**) or a new merge path (session→main vs. story→main), brainstorm must enumerate every \`.github/workflows/*.yml\` trigger filter that uses \`pull_request.branches\`, \`push.branches\`, or \`pull_request_target.branches\` and flag any filter that does NOT include the new pattern. The audit produces a checklist item: "Workflow X currently filters on [a, b]; under this epic, should it also include [new-pattern]? If yes, add to scope. If no, document why not."

#### Actual Behavior

Bug 3914-0848-faad-4f6a surfaced that ci.yml's \`pull_request.branches: [main]\` filter skipped every per-story PR introduced by f61f/d076, so per-story PRs ran LLM review and lint but no test coverage at all. d076's Cross-Epic Interactions section names ci.yml as overlapping but only the llm-review job was discussed; the test-running job's trigger filter was not audited.

### 3. Action History

Both f61f's and d076's brainstorms produced cross-resource scans (Step 2.27 and Cross-Epic Interactions); neither cross-scan enumerated workflow trigger filters. The current scan asks "which epics touch this resource" but not "which workflows trigger on this ref pattern."

### 4. Chronological Rationalization

User discovered the gap empirically when PR #166 ran only LLM review and lint, asking "why isn't PR 166 running any testing?" The gap should be a planning-stage check, not a runtime discovery.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

Affected skill: brainstorm (cross-resource scan Step 2.27 / Cross-Epic Interactions section). Suggested implementation: when the epic's deliverables include a new ref pattern, dispatch a haiku sub-task to enumerate \`.github/workflows/*.yml\` trigger filters and produce a delta report.

### 6. Logs

Reference: docs/findings/d076-postmortem-analysis.md §3 bug 3914 row + §6 row 2.
Working notes user intervention #10: "Why isn't PR 166 running any testing? It looks like it's only executing LLM review and lint."

comments.body: /dso:fix-bug BASIC investigation: brainstorm Step 2.27 (cross-resource scan) currently handles ambiguity/conflict resolution only — it does NOT audit new git ref patterns against existing .github/workflows/*.yml trigger filters. Proposed fix: add a workflow-trigger-filter audit step to Step 2.27 — when epic deliverables include a new git ref pattern, dispatch a haiku sub-agent to enumerate workflow trigger filters and flag any that would silently exclude the new ref. Classification: MODERATE — brainstorm SKILL.md addition + possibly skills/brainstorm/phases/cross-epic-handlers.md. Likely combines with jira-dig-2562 (same gap, focused on PR merge strategy changes). Not addressed in this P2 pass; leaving OPEN.
